source_evidence: International index funds seek to track the results of a particular foreign market or international market index. U.S.-registered ETFs can offer similar benefits as U.S.-registered mutual funds. In addition, ETFs are listed on stock exchanges and, like stocks (and in contrast to mutual funds), trade through the trading day with fluctuating market prices.
answer: An international index fund aims to track the results of a particular foreign market or international market index. U.S.-registered ETFs can offer benefits similar to U.S.-registered mutual funds, but ETFs trade on stock exchanges throughout the trading day, and their market prices can fluctuate during that day. These are different features to understand when learning about ways to get international investment exposure.
